title: Deleting a DM does not delete it, and the spec forbids leaving one
description:
Deleting a one-to-one conversation does not delete it, and room-policy-04 forbids the obvious fix. Mark asked for this as its own bead while deciding mimid-6vsk (adopt the deleted room in `open_direct`).

TODAY. `Store::forget_room` removes the record and leaves a `Tombstone::Room`. The agent stays in the MLS group and both users stay in the hub's participant list, so `Store::sync`'s `settle_forgotten_rooms` clears that tombstone as a "rejoined" room and `reconcile_rooms` makes a fresh empty record. `forget_room`'s own doc says so. A delete therefore lasts one sync interval.

WHAT THE SPEC SAYS, and it rules out the obvious fix. room-policy-04 §5: "Ordinary users cannot leave or be removed, however a user can remove all its clients from the associated MLS group. The most common case of a fixed-membership room is a 1:1 conversation." So a user cannot leave a DM. They can only take every client out of the MLS group, and they stay a participant.

WHICH MATTERS TWICE OVER. A user who is still a participant still matches the hub's `fixed_rooms_elsewhere` check, so a later message to that person cannot make a new room; the agent would have to rejoin the existing one by external Commit (it is still a participant, so it may: decision mimid-1wgh.61). And removing every client does make the delete durable, because the agent is then not active in the room and the sync has nothing to revive.

So the shape the spec points at is: delete means remove this user's clients from the group; writing to that person again means rejoining the room rather than hosting a new one. That is a different design from either reading on mimid-6vsk, and it is the one that makes a delete mean something.

A CONFORMANCE GAP SITS UNDER IT. Nothing in mimid enforces §5's "ordinary users cannot leave or be removed": crates/mimi-room-policy/src/lib.rs says that rule, with `max_clients`, `max_users` and `multi_device`, is "not checked here (room-policy-04 §5; decision mimid-1wgh.3.50)". The hub has no check either (grep for fixed_membership beside leave or remove in crates/mimid-server/src/hub finds nothing), and `Store::leave` does not refuse a direct room. So mimid currently lets an agent do what the spec says an ordinary user cannot, and bead mimid-5km1's finder assumed a leave works, which it does in mimid and should not.

WHAT NEEDS DECIDING. Whether a deleted DM should be durable at all, and if so whether it is done the spec's way (remove this user's clients, rejoin on the next message). Separately, whether mimid should enforce §5's rule it currently ignores, which is decision mimid-1wgh.3.50's to reopen, and which would make `Store::leave` refuse a fixed-membership room.
notes:
ANSWERED, Mark 2026-11-27 asked: "is this a bug in the mimi protocol? or do our c/s protocols have to clearly say 'leave this room' and 'leave this DM'?"

Not a protocol bug. room-policy-04 §5 is coherent, and protocol-07 completes it.

A fixed-membership room's identity is its participant set: that is the same rule that allows only one such room per set. A user who could leave would change the set, so the room would become a different room by the rule that identifies it, and a second room for the same pair could then exist. Forbidding the leave is what keeps one-room-per-pair meaningful. §5's escape hatch makes it usable: remove all your clients from the MLS group, stay a participant, receive nothing. protocol-07 (around line 854 of the -07 text) then gives the way back: the hub keeps or reconstructs the GroupInfo so a new client of an existing participant joins by External Commit. Identity immutable, delivery optional.

SO THE GAP IS OURS, and it is the distinction Mark named. Three things a user can mean, and mimid has names for two:

- "Hide this from me": local only, no wire effect. `Store::forget_room` and `Store::hide_room`. For a DM the next sync undoes it, which is bead mimid-6vsk's subject.
- "Stop sending this to my devices": remove all this user's clients from the MLS group, visible to the other party as a Commit, reversible by External Commit. mimid has no name for this.
- "Leave this group": remove this user as a participant. `Store::leave`, which is illegal for a fixed-membership room and which nothing in mimid refuses.

`Store::leave` conflating the last two is why bead mimid-5km1's finder concluded that deleting after leaving works: it does work in mimid, and per §5 it should not.

WHAT FOLLOWS, and this is the design the spec points at: a durable delete of a DM means removing this user's clients, and writing to that person again means rejoining the existing room by External Commit rather than hosting a new one. Never a new room.

STILL OPEN: what IRC does, since `PART` is its only word and cannot say which of the two a user meant; what the client-facing JMAP surface calls each of them; and whether mimi-room-policy should enforce §5's rule, which decision mimid-1wgh.3.50 deliberately left unchecked.

Nothing here needs the working group. If anything goes upstream it would be a question about what the hub owes a participant with no clients, and protocol-07's External Commit text may already answer it.
